description: Third-party (customer) MR sequences, recognized by the parameters they print on the Special card and by their sequence binary names. Curated by hand from real exports: a wrong entry reports a protocol as converting cleanly when it does not, so anything unaccounted for is reported as unrecognized rather than guessed at.

path_markers.CustomerSeq: site-installed sequence (Siemens writes this into the protocol path)

third_party_owners.USER: site-installed sequence (the export labels the binary USER, not SIEMENS)
third_party_owners.%CustomerSeq%: site-installed sequence (the protocol names its binary under the customer tree)

stock_owners.SIEMENS: the export labels the binary SIEMENS, naming the vendor as its owner
stock_owners.%SiemensSeq%: the protocol names its binary under the Siemens tree, not the customer one

stock_binaries.fl3d_rd: 3D FLASH, radial -- the kernel under VB17A's vessels_head angiography
stock_binaries.spcir: SPACE with inversion recovery -- FLAIR SPACE
stock_binaries.epfid: EPI, gradient-echo readout -- the kernel under ep2d_bold
stock_binaries.epse: EPI, spin-echo readout -- the kernel under ep2d_diff and ep2d_se
stock_binaries.ep2d_pace: product BOLD EPI with PACE prospective motion correction
stock_binaries.AALScout: AutoAlign scout -- the kernel under AAHead_Scout

signatures.note: The MB parameters are CMRR's own and appear on no Siemens kernel in any shipped example: 169 scans across VE11C, XA30 and XA60 print them, all of them epfid or epse. The kernel is what splits BOLD from diffusion, since both report a stock kernel name. On VB17A the sequence file name is printed instead and identifies it outright.

Same CMRR multiband card as cmrr-mb-epi-bold, riding on the spin-echo kernel. Seen on dMRI_dir64_MGH, dMRI_dir99 and ABCD_dMRI scans in VE11C, XA30 and XA60 exports. The MB card alone cannot say which variant this is -- BOLD and spin echo print it too -- so the Diff card carries the identification: a diffusion scan has to prescribe directions and b-values, so the console always prints it, where every Special-card label is a checkbox someone can clear. All 96 scans this matched before the clause print one, and nothing that is not diffusion prints one. VE11C splits it into Diff - Body, Diff - Neuro and Diff - Composing against Numaris/X's single Diff, which is why the match is on the card group at the head of the title rather than the page at its tail. Priority 25 puts it above cmrr-mb-epi-se, which is not needed for any corpus scan -- the two never both match today -- but makes the answer deliberate rather than a consequence of file order. If a diffusion protocol ever enables 'Triggering scheme', the option the SE entry keys on, the card it cannot help printing is the better evidence and should win.

Supplied by the protocols' owner. The third member of CMRR's multiband EPI family, on the spin-echo kernel like cmrr-mb-epi-diffusion, and the reason it needs two routes is that the two files say different things: an .exar1 names the sequence outright as cmrr_mbep2d_se, while a Numaris/X page prints only the kernel epse, which diffusion shares. Where both exist the archive is the better witness. On the page the two are told apart from opposite directions: diffusion is claimed positively by the Diff card it cannot help printing, and 'Triggering scheme' is on every one of the 17 SE scans a paired archive identifies and on none of the 23 diffusion scans, nor anywhere in their 22-label union. Of the 54 shipped scans this matches, an archive confirms 30 as cmrr_mbep2d_se and none as anything else.

signatures.family: EPI package (C2P), multiband off or not printed
signatures.note: These six labels are printed by 229 of the 230 epfid/epse scans that print a Special card at all, and by nothing else in any shipped example. They catch the CMRR spin-echo field maps -- SpinEchoFieldMap_AP/PA, CMRR_SEFieldMap, ABCD-SEFieldMap -- which run the same package with multiband disabled and so print no MB parameters. Lower priority than the multiband entries, which are the narrower answer when both match.
The vNav navigator parameters, on the multi-echo TurboFLASH kernel. Seen on T1w_MPR_vNav_4e and T1_MEMPRAGE_1.0mm_p4_vNav in XA30 exports.

signatures.family: navigated T2 SPACE (vNav prospective motion correction)
signatures.note: The same vNav navigator parameters as vnav-mprage, on the SPACE kernel. Seen on ABCD_T2w_SPC_vNav (XA30) and T2_SPACE_GSP_vNavTrk (VE11C). Plain spc scans print an empty Special card, which is what separates the navigated variant from the stock one.

signatures.family: vNav prospective motion correction, base sequence unread
signatures.note: The vNav navigator without a readable kernel to say which sequence carries it. One XA30 export prints T1w_MEMPR_vNav with no sequence field at all, and this is what still identifies it. Reported with the base sequence called out as unknown rather than assumed to be MPRAGE.

MEMPRAGE without the vNav navigator. Its four labels are disjoint from the vNav set, so the two tfl_me variants separate cleanly: 18 scans named T1_MEMPRAGE_64ch or MEMPRAGE across VE11C, XA30 and XA60. VB17A prints the sequence file name tfl_mgh_multiecho instead, on scans named me_mprage and T1_mprage_mgh.

Deelchand's semi-LASER, and one of two distinct semi-LASER sequences from CMRR -- see cmrr-semilaser for Auerbach's. Supplied by the protocols' owner; the corpus is overwhelmingly this one, 421 scans in the whole-scanner export against 7 of the other. Three spellings because the two files and the two releases each name it differently: a VE11C page prints the kernel sead, a Numaris/X page prints slaser, and an .exar1 prints the sequence file name svs_slaser_dkd. That rename across releases is exactly the kind of thing that breaks a conversion, so the parameter fingerprint rather than the binary is what identifies it on a page. Its card shares only 'Inversion pulse' with Auerbach's, which is why the two cannot be confused: this one prints GOIA/FOCI and FA AutoCalib, and that one the OVS and VAPOR blocks.

Auerbach's semi-LASER, supplied by the protocols' owner and distinct from Deelchand's dkd-semilaser despite both coming from CMRR. The kernels are one character apart and easy to confuse -- Auerbach's prints slasr where Deelchand's prints slaser -- but the cards are unmistakable: this one prints the OVS and VAPOR blocks and 39 labels in all, none of which appear on any Deelchand scan. Only 7 scans in the whole-scanner export run it. The same kernel and very nearly the same card also serve the CSI variant, eja_csi_slaser: an .exar1 names the two apart and a page does not, their Special cards sharing 39 of 40 labels. What separates them is the Resolution card, which prints a phase-encoding matrix only when there is one -- absent on all 27 single-voxel spectroscopy scans in the corpus and 8 or 16 on all 6 CSI ones, with nothing against. The bound is 'at most 1' rather than 'absent' because a 1 x 1 matrix would mean the same thing; the corpus shows only absence.

The chemical-shift-imaging variant of cmrr-semilaser, and the same author's: an .exar1 names it eja_csi_slaser beside eja_svs_slaser, and a page prints the kernel slasr and the same 39 Special-card labels for both. Only the Resolution card tells them apart, which is what the two entries key on -- this one requires a phase-encoding matrix of at least 2 where the single-voxel entry allows at most 1, so the pair partitions and a scan printing a 1 goes to that one alone. Every CSI spectroscopy scan in the corpus prints 8 or 16 and every single-voxel one prints none, so the bound sits in a gap the corpus never occupies.

Auerbach's MEGA-edited semi-LASER, supplied by the protocols' owner and a different sequence from his MEGA-PRESS -- which is why cmrr-megapress is gated to the mpres kernel and no longer claims these. Its own kernel is mslsr, unique to it in the corpus, and its card is exactly the pair of techniques its name says: the MEGA editing labels that MEGA-PRESS also prints, over the semi-LASER refocusing block -- GOIA refoc. pulses, HS refoc. pulse N and R -- that MEGA-PRESS does not. Keying on one of each is what makes the fingerprint name this sequence rather than either technique. Both the single-voxel and the CSI spelling are listed for the archive route; they are not split the way the plain semi-LASER is, because the owner named them together.

Auerbach's PRESS, supplied by the protocols' owner, in its single-voxel and CSI spellings -- 136 and 6 scans in the whole-scanner export. They share the entry rather than being split the way the semi-LASERs are, because the owner named them together; the Resolution card would separate them if wanted, since the CSI scans print a 16 x 16 matrix and the single-voxel ones none. Three of the 22 labels every eja sequence prints -- the VAPOR water-suppression delays and the timing controls -- so the card says this is Auerbach's implementation and the kernel says which technique. That division is why the kernel gate is not optional here: PRESS, LASER and STEAM are techniques anyone may implement, and it is the pairing that names a sequence.

Auerbach's LASER, supplied by the protocols' owner, in both spellings. Its card carries the GOIA and hyperbolic-secant refocusing controls that the semi-LASER entries also print -- the two techniques share their refocusing train -- so the kernel is what tells them apart. Three of the 22 labels every eja sequence prints -- the VAPOR water-suppression delays and the timing controls -- so the card says this is Auerbach's implementation and the kernel says which technique. That division is why the kernel gate is not optional here: PRESS, LASER and STEAM are techniques anyone may implement, and it is the pairing that names a sequence.

Auerbach's STEAM, supplied by the protocols' owner. Only the single-voxel spelling is named; the corpus also holds eja_svs_steam_diff, which is not claimed here because nobody has said what it is. Three of the 22 labels every eja sequence prints -- the VAPOR water-suppression delays and the timing controls -- so the card says this is Auerbach's implementation and the kernel says which technique. That division is why the kernel gate is not optional here: PRESS, LASER and STEAM are techniques anyone may implement, and it is the pairing that names a sequence.

Auerbach's eja_svs_mpress; the eja_ prefix is CMRR's spectroscopy suite. Both spellings are listed because the two files name the sequence differently: a page prints the kernel mpres, an .exar1 prints the sequence file name eja_svs_mpress. They are the same sequence, joined archive-to-printout on five scans in Frederick_P2 -- same scan names, kernel mpres, and both Special-card labels present on every one. The kernel gate is what keeps it to MEGA-PRESS. Its two card labels are editing parameters that any MEGA-edited sequence prints, so ungated the card route also claimed three mslsr scans -- eja_svs_mslaser and eja_csi_mslaser -- and MEGA-semi-LASER is a different sequence, per the protocols' owner. Those are unrecognized now rather than misattributed, which is the honest state until someone names them.

Gruetter's FASTMAP/FASTESTMAP shim sequence, which fits field projections along columns -- hence the bar geometry parameters. Ten scans across VE11C and XA60, every one named fastestmap. Confirmed by the protocol's owner.

signatures.family: SPICE -- spectroscopic imaging by exploiting spatiospectral correlation
signatures.note: The ZPL_ binary prefix is the author's initials; the shipped examples carry four of them -- ZPL_epsi_fid, ZPL_epsi_fid_v1h, ZPL_epsi_se_v1b, ZPL_JPSI_se -- running scans named ZPL_RG_EPSI_*, in protocols named *_SPICE_*. Its Special card is the widest of any sequence here, and the sampling-table file name it prints is the value that once collapsed the value column; see columns.value_origin.

signatures.family: navigator setter -- establishes the baseline location for navigated scans
signatures.note: Sets the baseline head position that the vNav scans later navigate back to, so it acquires no images of its own -- which is why it prints exactly one Special parameter, Protocol filename. Eighteen scans across VE11C, XA30 and XA60, every one named *_setter. It is site-installed and does not survive a release change, so it belongs on the rebuild list; and because the navigated scans depend on it, rebuilding those without it is not enough.

CMRR's multiband ASL. Seen as the mbPCASL binary on VE11C and, on XA60, as an epfid scan named mbPCASLhr that prints only the three labeling parameters -- too few to match the CMRR EPI package entry, which needs six, so the labeling parameters have to identify it themselves. Siemens' product ASL in these releases is ep2d_pasl, pulsed rather than pseudo-continuous.

VB17A only, by sequence file name -- ep2d_DE_pcasl_iPAT, running eighteen scans named pcasl_DE_*. The DE is the dual echo. Confirmed third-party by the export's USER owner label; the group that wrote it is not recorded, so the vendor is left unattributed rather than guessed.
VB17A only, and identified by the sequence file name alone, since VB17A prints no Special card. Ten scans named VASO_flipback_*.
VB17A only, by sequence file name -- a modified ep2d_se for vascular-space-occupancy CBV imaging. Attribution is from the protocol's owner; no export states it.
VB17A only, by sequence file name -- ep2d_bold_MGH_tb. One scan in the shipped examples.

Collaborative VASO sequence development with Laurentius (Renzo) Huber based on the custom DZNE skipped-CAIPI 3D-EPI sequence (segmented acquisition with CAIPIRINHA sampling). This sequence is compatible with FRISGO and NORDIC. The binary prints as 'vso rslh6.0' and the archive names the sequence file rslh_ep3d_vaso, so the printed string carries a build number that a later release would change -- which is why the Special card is listed too, and why the three VASO Pre-* delays are the ones chosen: they name the technique rather than the EPI readout it shares with everything else on that card.
